summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — ACN +16%, SNPS +13%, FICO +12%, COHR +11%, CIEN +8%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (CTVA -84%, PSKY -10%, MKC -5%, DHR -4%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: CTVA (-83.81%) — Not a real loss: Corteva completed the spin-off of its seed business as Vylor (VYLR) on Oct 1, 2026, one share per CTVA share. The -83.81% is the ex-distribution price reset, not an adjusted price drop. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe. CTVA is a mid/large-cap ag-chemicals name that no strategy includes. Even if it had been included, a corporate-action price drop with no adjustment looks like a gap that gap/RSI filters would reject.

top_movers.catalyst: FQ4 earnings beat (EPS $3.29 vs $3.18, revenue $18.68B vs $18.03B est.), record bookings, a higher dividend and a $1B Anthropic AI partnership eased AI-disruption fears. Stock peaked above +22% intraday.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. ACN is a large-cap IT-services name that no strategy lists. The jump was a pre-market earnings gap, so a post-open momentum or news-reactive entry would have been late and chasing a ~16–22% gap.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap IT-services/consulting names (ACN, IBM, CTSH) to the news-reactive universe, and let the earnings-gate release names that gap up ≥+8% on record-bookings or beat-and-raise results within 30 minutes of the open.

top_movers.catalyst: Investor Day: >$1B multiyear Amazon deal, OpenAI 'GPT-Synopsys' partnership, FY27 guidance (~$11.1-11.2B rev, EPS ~$19.1) above consensus, plus HSBC upgrade to Buy (PT $700).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: SNPS is a large-cap software/EDA name that no strategy lists. The move was also a single-session event-driven gap from an Investor Day, so a post-event momentum signal would have come too late.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a gap-scanner sleeve that admits any S&P 500 / Nasdaq-100 name gapping ≥+5% on ≥2× average volume at the open, bypassing the static universe list, with a stop at the open-gap low.

top_movers.catalyst: FICO rebounded ~12% after FHFA Director Pulte approved its Direct License Program, which lets it sell mortgage credit scores directly to lenders. This followed a ~27% drop earlier in the week on VantageScore competition.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: FICO is a ~$16B mid/large-cap data/analytics name that no strategy lists. It was also a policy-headline rebound after a crash, so a gap-up or RSI filter would likely have excluded it even if it were in the universe.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a dynamic 'extreme-mover' watchlist that admits any name with a ≥±10% close-to-close move on ≥2× 20-day average volume into the news-reactive strategy's universe for the next session, with a reduced position size cap.

top_movers.catalyst: Bernstein initiated coverage with Outperform and a $350 target, calling optical networking a structural AI winner. Lumentum and Ciena also rallied, and PhotonLink got attention. Coverage dates the ~10-11% jump to Oct 1, so the date is unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: COHR is a ~$50B mid/large-cap AI-optics name that no strategy lists. The move was an analyst-initiation and sector rerating that built intraday, so no pre-market gap or earnings signal would have triggered a news-reactive bot.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an 'ai_optics' basket (COHR, LITE, CIEN, GLW) to the momentum-trader universe, or let it admit any S&P 500/400 name with 1-day return ≥ +5% and volume ≥ 2× its 20-day average.

top_movers.catalyst: AI optical-networking rally: Evercore ISI Outperform and bullish sector research, on top of strong fiscal Q3 results (revenue +37%, $8.5B backlog, cloud customers 53% of revenue). No fresh company-specific event found.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CIEN is a mid/large-cap optical-networking name (about $379 a share) that no strategy's universe list includes. The move was a gradual analyst and sector re-rating, with no earnings gap for a news-reactive filter to catch.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a dynamic universe slot that admits any US stock with a ≥5% daily gain and above-average volume (e.g. 1.5× the 20-day average) for the next session, so momentum-trader can evaluate AI-infrastructure names like CIEN without a hand-curated list.

top_movers.catalyst: AI-optics rally: Lumentum showed AI optical hardware ahead of ECOC 2026 and speaks at OCP Summit, and sell-side notes (Barclays) cite faster co-packaged optics/OCS deployment. Stock is up about 170% YTD.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: LITE is a roughly $70B+ AI-optical-networking mid/large-cap with a ~$1,000 share price. It probably failed a price or market-cap filter, and after a 170% YTD run an RSI/extension filter would exclude it anyway.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'high-priced AI-infrastructure momentum' sleeve (optical/networking names like LITE, COHR, CIEN) and drop any max share price cap. Use fractional or notional sizing and raise the RSI ceiling to about 85 when the sector's 20-day relative strength is positive.

top_movers.catalyst: Not a real loss: Corteva completed the spin-off of its seed business as Vylor (VYLR) on Oct 1, 2026, one share per CTVA share. The -83.81% is the ex-distribution price reset, not an adjusted price drop.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. CTVA is a mid/large-cap ag-chemicals name that no strategy includes. Even if it had been included, a corporate-action price drop with no adjustment looks like a gap that gap/RSI filters would reject.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a corporate-action guard to the mover/screening pipeline. Flag any single-day |move| > 40% with no news, or an 8-K spin-off or ex-date, as 'distribution artifact' and exclude it from loser lists and signals. Use split/dividend-adjusted closes.

top_movers.catalyst: Paramount priced a $41.4B debt package (secured notes plus an $8.5B term loan) to fund its Warner Bros. Discovery buyout. S&P cut its rating to BB, and some bond yields are above 10%. The stock fell despite antitrust clearance.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: PSKY is a roughly $10B-cap, low-priced media stock. The move came from a deal-financing and credit-downgrade event, not a technical setup. A long-only momentum or mean-reversion bot has no short entry for it.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change. This is a deal-financing and credit event on a stock outside the universe, and it needs short capability the bot lacks. Optionally, log M&A-financing losers (-8% or worse on 3x volume) to a watchlist, but don't trade them.

top_movers.catalyst: MKC fell 4.9% to a new 52-week low (~$44) after the Q3 results, with weak 2% organic growth, flat Consumer Americas and margin pressure. TD Cowen cut its price target from $55 to $48.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: MKC is a mid-cap consumer-staples name. The drop was a post-earnings fundamental de-rating and a slow slide to 52-week lows, so a momentum or news-reactive entry would have had no pre-market signal. The bot is also probably long-only.
top_movers.suggestion: (no actionable change; this is a long-only bot and a staples de-rating would need short capability.) If a tweak is wanted, add S&P 500 staples to the mean-reversion universe, gated by a 'no entry within 3 days of a post-earnings gap ≤ -4%' rule.

top_movers.catalyst: CEO transition took effect: Julie Sawyer Montgomery replaced Rainer Blair as CEO. The stock fell 4.4% to 211.76 amid worries about execution risk and weak biopharma capex before Q3 results. No fresh fundamental news.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. DHR is a large-cap life-sciences tools name that no strategy's universe includes. The move was a slow, sentiment-driven drift down (about -5% on the week) with no gap or volume spike, so momentum and news filters would not have flagged it either.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change: a long-only bot can't express a downside move in a name outside its universe. Optionally add large-cap healthcare tools (DHR, TMO, A) to the mean-reversion universe, gated on RSI<30 near the 52-week low.
